title: CRLR/509/2022 of PANKAJ BONTHIYAL Vs PRIYANKA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 509 of 2022
Pankaj Bonthiyal ....Revisionist
Vs.
Priyanka and Another ..... Respondents
Mr. Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta assisted by Ms. Irum Zeba, Advocates for
the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The challenge in this revision is made to
the order of interim maintenance dated 29.06.2022,
passed in Misc. Criminal Case No. 35 of 2022, Priyanka
Vs. Pankaj Bonthiyal, by the Family Court, Kotdwar,
District Pauri Garhwal ("the case"). By the impugned
judgment and order, an application, filed by the
respondent no.1, under Section 125 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code"), has been allowed
and the revisionist has been directed to pay Rs. 7,000/-
per month as maintenance.
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist
and perused the record.

2
3. Perusal of the record reveals that the
revisionist and the respondent no.1 married on
03.02.2017. According to the respondent no.1, the
revisionist and his family members demanded additional
dowry and for that reason, she was harassed, abused
and denied meals. Even, according to the respondent
no.1, the revisionist would commit marpeet from her.
She was expelled from her house. The respondent no.1
filed an application under Section 125 of the Code
seeking maintenance from the revisionist.
4. The revisionist filed his objections in the
case. According to him, it is the respondent no.1, who
would threaten the revisionist to implicate him in false
cases, saying that she wanted to marry with some other
person, but she was forcibly made to marry with the
revisionist. She would take fight quite often. She is a
woman of independent thoughts. She wanted to live in
independence. She had deserted the company of the
revisionist without any reasonable cause. The
revisionist has ever been ready and willing to keep the
respondent no.1 with him as his wife and discharge his
marital obligations. She was never abused, threatened
and harassed for whatsoever reasons. According to the
revisionist, on 07.08.2017, on Raksha Bandhan, the

3
respondent no.1 left her matrimonial house and went to
her father's house. On 28.08.2017, she again tried to
abuse the family members of the revisionist. She would
threaten the revisionist and his family members to
implicate in false cases and left the matrimonial house.
Despite repeated requests of the revisionist, the
respondent no.1 did not return.
5. Both the parties adduce evidence in the
case. After hearing the parties, by the impugned
judgment and order, the application under Section 125
of the Code has been allowed and the revisionist has
been directed to pay Rs. 7,000/- per month as
maintenance.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist , at the
very outset, would submit that it is a matrimonial
dispute. The court should be not much strict and rigid
in such cases. There may always be chances of
amicable settlement between the parties. It is submitted
that the revisionist is ever ready and willing to keep the
respondent no.1 as his wife with him and to discharge
the marital obligations. Learned counsel for the
revisionist also raised the following points in his
submission:-

4
(i) According to the respondent no.1,
she was expelled from her
matrimonial house on 27.08.2017,
but the respondent no.1 did not
even report to the police or gave any
notice to the revisionist with regard
to any force or forcible eviction.
(ii) In the month of December, 2017, the
revisionist visited the paternal
house of the respondent no.1, but
the respondent no.1 refused to join
the company of the revisionist.
(iii) The respondent no.1 wanted to
marry some other person. For that
reason, she would abuse and take
fights on small issues with the
revisionist and his family members
(iv) The respondent no.1, on her own,
without any reasonable cause,
deserted the revisionist. Therefore,
she is not entitled to maintenance.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist also
referred to the alleged telephonic conversation between
the revisionist and the respondent no.1, which is filed as

5
Annexure-4 to the revision to indicate that the
respondent no.1 has admitted that she was never
harassed for the demand of dowry.
8. It is a revision. The scope is much
restricted to the extent of examining the error, legality or
propriety of the impugned judgment and order. Of
course, in the matrimonial cases, the court should make
endeavour so that parties may amicably settle the
dispute and may not spare much of their precious time
of life in multiple litigation. But then, every case, arising
out from matrimonial dispute, may not be accepted in
this Court with the hope that parties may perhaps arrive
at a settlement. There should be reasons to make any
interference in the revision. The Court proceeds to
examine the issue.
9. It is true that the respondent no.1, in her
cross-examination, has stated that after the revisionist
expelled her from his house on 27.08.2017, she did not
lodge any report. This statement has even been referred
to in Para 11 of the impugned judgment. In this
sequence, the respondent no.1 has also stated that if the
revisionist takes her with him, she is ready to stay with
him.

6
10. On the one hand, the respondent no.1 has
admitted that she did not lodge any report against the
revisionist with regard to forcible expulsion from the
house, but when the Court posed a question to learned
counsel for the revisionist as to what attempt was made
by the revisionist in terms of legal proceedings to take
his wife with him, learned counsel for the revisionist
would submit that the revisionist visited the house of the
respondent no.1 to take her back, but she refused.
Admittedly, the revisionist also did not file any suit for
restitution of conjugal rights, she was also not given any
notice. In Para 12 of the impugned judgment, the court
has discussed this aspect. The court observed that it is
not established that the revisionist made any bona fide
attempt to take the respondent no.1 with him.
11. A telephonic conversation has been
referred to, which is Annexure 4 to the revision. Learned
counsel for the revisionist admits that this telephonic
conversation was not filed in the court below. How can
such conversation may be taken into consideration to
examine the legality, error or impropriety of the
impugned judgment? When requested to explain it,
learned counsel for the revisionist would submit that
strictly speaking, it cannot be considered at this stage.

7
12. The telephonic conversation has been filed
in the Court to show that the respondent no.1 accepted,
in her conversation with the revisionist that she was not
harassed. The husband is speaking to his wife and
recording the conversation without letting the wife know.
Does it mean that the husband wanted to extract
something from the wife? Is it a structured
conversation? Even otherwise, if this conversation is
read, it speaks that, in fact, the respondent no.1 was
harassed, taunted, in her matrimonial house. In answer
to one question, she stated, "pareshan nahi kia par
sunaya tha..." In another answer, she says, "bike ke
liye bola tha, humne pucha tha apse apko bike
chahaye ya nahi?" and at other place, she would say,
"aap logo se pucha tha na apko aur kya chaheye par
apke ghar me rakhne ki jagah he nahi thi, account
me paisa pade the jo ke kaha tha bhavishaye me
kaam ayega...".
13. The court below has appreciated the
evidence and arrived at a conclusion. The court below
has analysed the reasons of staying separate by the
respondent no.1. Para 11 onwards, the discussion has
been made in the impugned judgment and at Para 14,

8
the court concluded that the respondent no.1 has been
able to establish that she has sufficient cause and
reasons to stay separate. This finding cannot be said to
be perverse. It is not that admissible evidence has not
been considered or any irrelevant material has been
considered or any material evidence has not been
considered.
14. In view of it, this Court does not see any
reason to make any interference. The revision has no
merit and it deserves to be dismissed at the stage of
admission itself.
15. The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 06.09.2022 Ravi Bisht
